dicas.texto: Você está indo bem! Pense: quantas vezes o denominador 5 cabe dentro do numerador 6?
Tente dividir o numerador pelo denominador. O quociente será a parte inteira (m1) e o que sobrar será o novo numerador (m2).
O número inteiro (m1) é 1. Agora, quanto sobra de 6 se você já tirou 5? Esse resto vai no numerador da fração (m2).
Você tem 6/5. Como 5/5 é igual a 1 inteiro, sobra 1/5. Preencha m1 com 1, m2 com 1 e mantenha o denominador m3 como 5.
Onde fica o número 1 na reta? Como a fração é 1 e um pouquinho, o ponto deve estar à direita ou à esquerda do 1?
A reta está dividida em 5 partes. Cada marca pequena representa 1/5. Conte uma marca após o número 1.
Localize o 1 na reta. O ponto deve ficar exatamente na primeira marca após o 1.
Como o denominador é 5, cada espaço entre os números inteiros tem 5 divisões. Coloque o ponto na primeira divisão logo após o número 1.

Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you." com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); botão "Convert" que abre as caixas do número misto (m1 = parte inteira, m2/m3 = fração restante; "-" quando não há); reta numérica de 0 a 2 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 5 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. passos.acao: In the top fraction box, enter the numerator: the number of gum pieces Brandon gave Luke.
In the bottom fraction box, enter the denominator: the number of pieces in one pack.
Use the rightFraction display to identify whether the fraction is greater than 1.
Click Convert, then fill the mixed-number fields with the whole part and the remaining fraction.
On numline, mark 6/5: the first fifth after 1.
Click Done to submit the fraction and its location on the number line.

dicas.texto: Which number tells how many pieces Brandon gave away?
For a fraction describing pieces of a pack, place the amount given away in the top position.
Look at the sentence that tells how many pieces Brandon gave Luke.
Enter the number of pieces given away in f1, the top fraction field.
What number describes one complete pack of gum?
The denominator tells how many equal pieces make one whole pack.
Use the number in the sentence describing each pack.
Enter the number of pieces in one pack in f2, the bottom fraction field.
Compare the amount given away with the amount needed for one complete pack.
A fraction is ... when its numerator is greater than its denominator.
The top number counts the given pieces, while the bottom number counts the pieces in one pack.
In rightFraction, select the comparison showing that the numerator represents more than one whole denominator group.
A mixed number shows complete groups first and leftover pieces second.
Divide the numerator by the denominator; the quotient is the whole part and the remainder becomes the new numerator.
Find how many complete groups of five fit into six, then determine how many pieces remain.
Click Convert, enter the number of complete groups in m1, enter the leftover pieces in m2, and keep the pack size as m3.
Use the denominator to determine how each whole is divided on the number line.
Locate 1 first, then move forward by the fraction represented by one of the equal intervals.
The number line divides each unit into five equal parts, so count one fifth beyond 1.
Place the point on the first hidden subdivision to the right of the 1 mark.
Before submitting, check that the fraction and its point describe the same amount.
Review the numerator, denominator, mixed-number fields, and marked position in order.
The point should be just beyond 1, at the first of the five equal subdivisions.
Confirm the marked point is one fifth after 1, then click Done.

exercicio.statement:
Brandon had packs of gum that he shared with his friend. Each pack had five pieces. He gave Luke six pieces. Describe the number of packs of gum Brandon gave away and show the value on the number line.
What is the fraction in the problem? Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you.

In the bottom fraction box, enter the denominator: the number of pieces in one pack.
Use the rightFraction display to identify whether the fraction is greater than 1.
Click Convert, then fill the mixed-number fields with the whole part and the remaining fraction.
On numline, mark 6/5: the first fifth after 1.
Click Done to submit the fraction and its location on the number line.

hints.message: Use the denominator to determine how each whole is divided on the number line.
Locate 1 first, then move forward by the fraction represented by one of the equal intervals.
The number line divides each unit into five equal parts, so count one fifth beyond 1.
Place the point on the first hidden subdivision to the right of the 1 mark.

hints.message: Before submitting, check that the fraction and its point describe the same amount.
Review the numerator, denominator, mixed-number fields, and marked position in order.
The point should be just beyond 1, at the first of the five equal subdivisions.
Confirm the marked point is one fifth after 1, then click Done.
